title: Training Frontier Models to Out-Think Hackers — Uri Rolls, Arithmetic & Thom Wolf, Hugging Face
talk_summary: Arithmetic and Hugging Face present a cybersecurity benchmark (Masov) focused on access-control logic vulnerabilities, where agents must reason across chained blackbox environments to find multi-step privilege-escalation exploits. The core methodological contribution is deterministic step-level grading of long agent trajectories plus human-curated out-of-distribution tasks, rather than end-to-end pass/fail.

takeaways.technique: Deterministic step-level partial graders on agent trajectories
takeaways.what_they_do: Every step in the exploitation chain is deterministically verified, so they can measure how deep an agent got even when it fails the final binary task.
takeaways.evidence_quote: every single step can be deterministically verified, allowing us to see how deep it got within the chain
takeaways.numbers: only one solve at K1; at K5 only GPT solves

takeaways.what_they_do: Human vulnerability researchers find real zero-days in widely-used OSS and build tasks around them, so the eval contains genuinely novel cases models can't pattern-match.
takeaways.evidence_quote: our data is created first by humans ... to find out of distribution things we need humans to go do the search

takeaways.technique: Blackbox environment forcing world-model reasoning over pattern matching
takeaways.what_they_do: Models get no codebase or internet access, only tooling, and must build a dynamic model of a chained system to find logic breaks between components.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we don't give it access to the internet or the codebase, but we do give it sort of all the basic tooling

takeaways.technique: Trace-level failure-mode analysis as a routine
takeaways.what_they_do: The researcher spends the day reading full agent traces to identify specific failure modes and where the model failed to make a logical leap.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the way I spend all my day is is quite literally going through all the traces of what the models did, why, and how
takeaways.numbers: a run working over three hours still unable to solve

takeaways.technique: Capability-leap profiling per model, not aggregate scores
takeaways.what_they_do: They measure which specific reasoning leaps each model can make, showing most models capture discovery info but fail the exploitation leap.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they do capture nearly all the different information they need and they never are able to make the leap

takeaways.technique: Isolated reproducible environments with solve scripts
takeaways.what_they_do: Each task ships with a real environment and a solve script showing a valid solution path, enabling deterministic replay and grading.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Each one of our tasks has a solve script of what a real solution looks like
